releaseNotes:
## Downloads

- macOS 14 or later, Apple Silicon: signed, notarized and stapled Developer ID installer (`.pkg`).
- Windows 10/11, x64: unsigned NSIS installer (`.exe`) with optional NVIDIA CUDA support; installation is manual. The installer now shows its pages in your Windows display language (English when there is no match).
- Linux x64: two `.deb` packages for Debian/Ubuntu amd64, built on Ubuntu 20.04 (glibc 2.31 or later):
  - `crossdesk-linux-amd64-v1.7.7-4-20261128.deb`: the standard package, uses the existing desktop session.
  - the `virtual-desktop-xfce` package: the same app, and APT also installs Xvfb, Xfce and the D-Bus session tools for hosts without a desktop.

  Install only one of the two with `sudo apt install ./<package>.deb`.
- Verify the downloads with `SHA256SUMS.txt`.

## Upgrading

- From v1.7.7-3: the in-app updater offers this release.
- From v1.7.7-1 or v1.7.7-2: those versions only trust the old feed key, so install v1.7.7-3 or this release by hand once. Later releases arrive in the app again.

## Changes

This release is based on upstream CrossDesk `mcp` at `26b56503` ("[perf] use native macOS frame scaling from MiniRTC"). It is not an upstream release: upstream has not tagged a version since v1.7.7-20261124.

Upstream changes since v1.7.7-3:
- New languages: Turkish and Hebrew (right-to-left).
- IP direct connections accept hostnames (including `.local` names). A saved password is bound to the host's identity, and CrossDesk warns when that identity changes. Translated VPN addresses work.
- Remote connections show their progress, signaling is checked again after the computer wakes, and wired network paths are preferred.
- Screen capture is paced to the viewer's frame rate on Windows, macOS and Linux, with faster capture paths on Windows (DXGI, Intel Quick Sync) and macOS.
- Headless Macs can use Snug virtual displays; the HiDPI mode and display layout are restored after reconnects and wake.
- Device groups can be renamed and managed from the group dialogs.
- Keyboard and pointer fixes: Caps Lock on macOS, Shift with pointer gestures, horizontal scrolling, key releases and pointer control across Windows display changes.
- The Windows service repairs its machine identity folder permissions, retained tray icons are recovered, and the autostart migration finishes for every user on a shared machine.
- Updates are protected against two users updating at once on macOS and Linux. The unused macOS camera and microphone permissions are gone.

CrossDesk Postcard changes:
- The connection window fits small or scaled displays, for example 1366x768 at 125% (https://github.com/thuongtin/crossdesk/pull/6).
- A Mac host whose display was asleep now wakes it when a viewer connects, so the viewer no longer waits on a black "Receiving screen..." view. If there is still no picture, the viewer explains why: missing screen recording permission, a sleeping display, or a capture failure (https://github.com/thuongtin/crossdesk/pull/8).
- Settings: in-row buttons are centered and no longer cross the row divider; several dialogs opened from Settings no longer cut off their buttons or logo (https://github.com/thuongtin/crossdesk/pull/9).
- The Windows installer is no longer Chinese only: it follows the Windows display language in 13 languages, and new installations go to `C:\Program Files\CrossDesk`. Existing installations are upgraded in place (https://github.com/thuongtin/crossdesk/pull/10).
- Linux UI text uses the system sans-serif font; v1.7.7-3 rendered Latin text in a serif font (https://github.com/thuongtin/crossdesk/pull/13).
- The Vietnamese translation covers all new strings, and on macOS and Linux a hostname listed in `/etc/hosts` is used before DNS (https://github.com/thuongtin/crossdesk/pull/7).
- Keeps Postcard, DeskHub, the fork update channel and English as the default for new installs. The default signaling endpoint remains `crossdesk.ecom.io.vn:9099`. The GitHub button in **Feedback & suggestions** stays removed: export the logs there and send the ZIP to your CrossDesk administrator.
